title: Async Code Must Not Block
goal: Keep worker threads free by avoiding synchronous blocking calls in async functions.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Async Pitfalls

sections.text: Async tasks share a small pool of worker threads. When an async task calls a blocking function like `std::thread::sleep`, that thread stops doing any work for all other tasks assigned to it.

sections.caption: std::thread::sleep halts the entire OS thread.

sections.text: An async function should yield execution back to the runtime while waiting. Use non-blocking timers like `tokio::time::sleep` that return a future instead of blocking.

sections.caption: sleep().await pauses only this task, letting others run.

sections.text: If you must run CPU-heavy or blocking I/O code, offload it using `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. That moves the blocking work onto a dedicated thread pool managed by the runtime.

explanation: Keep worker threads free by avoiding synchronous blocking calls in async functions.
